en: The Triplet on the Visible (Sanidassanattika) and the Couplet on the Clung-to (Upādinnaduka).
Dependent on a state that is non-manifesting, non-reacting, and grasped, there arises a state that is neither non-manifesting nor non-reacting and is not grasped,

by way of root condition. Dependent on a state that is non-manifesting, non-reacting, and grasped, there arises a state that is neither non-manifesting nor with resistance and is not grasped, by way of root condition … [and so on] … dependent on a state that is non-manifesting, non-reacting, and grasped.

Dependent on states that are non-visible and non-reacting, as well as non-clung-to and non-non-visible and non-reacting, there arise states that are non-visible and non-reacting, as well as non-clung-to and non-non-visible and non-reacting, by way of root condition.
(Abbreviated. There are six [conditions] in the case of root;
six each in the cases of conascence, dependence, kamma, resultant, nutriment, faculty, jhāna, path, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance.

A phenomenon that is visible, impinging, and not acquired by clinging (*anupādinna*) is a condition, by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*), for a phenomenon that is invisible, non-impinging, and not acquired by clinging. (Abbreviated. There are nine [conditions] in the case of the object;

three each in the cases of the proximate, the immediate, the decisive support, and the prenascence; six in the case of kamma; nine in the case of presence; three each in the cases of absence and disappearance; and nine in the case of non-disappearance.
